solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Lord having no right to accept jibe about ancestry

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the remaining letters hold the next pieces
the R, abbreviation for right, is dropped from the word for lord

parts.note: a lord is a peer of the realm
a dig is a jibe or snide remark
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A haughty nobleman, mocked for his lineage, is short of a right-hand ally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lord' tempts as the definition of a noble line, but it is wordplay; 'having no right' removes one R, and 'to accept' wraps what is left round the jibe and 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedigree is a recorded line of descent, so it means lineage or ancestry.

clue.text: Having more than one place on river

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names
the Ural is a river flowing from Russia through Kazakhstan

explanation.surface: Someone owns several homes, including one beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link word: in a down answer the place abbreviation sits on top of the river.
explanation.definitionFit: A plural word refers to more than one, so plural means having more than one.

clue.text: Told he can broadcast series of events

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A man is told he may transmit a run of fixtures on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' looks like television, but signals rearranging the letters of 'Told he can'.
explanation.definitionFit: The decathlon is an athletics competition made up of ten separate events.

clue.text: Book band or creative event

definitions.meaning: the first book of the Bible
an English rock group of the 1970s and 1980s
the coming into being of something, its origin or creation

explanation.surface: A list of options: a volume, a music group, or an act of creation.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis names the Bible's opening book, a famous rock band, and the origin or beginning of anything.

clue.text: Host starts to make conversation audibly

indicators.note: audibly means as heard, so the letters are spelt out as they are spoken

parts.note: the starts of the words make and conversation are M and C

explanation.surface: A party host begins chatting so everyone can hear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' gives M and C, the initials of master of ceremonies; 'audibly' spells those initials as they sound.
explanation.definitionFit: An emcee is a master of ceremonies, who presents or hosts an event or show.

clue.text: Read novel receiving the author's backing and respect

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the shuffled letters hold the next piece
novel means new or fresh, so the letters of read are given a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so I'm is read backwards

parts.note: the setter is the author, so 'the author's' is I'm, short for I am

explanation.surface: A reader is urged to study a novel with the writer's support and some esteem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Read novel' looks like advice about books; 'novel' rearranges the letters of Read, and the setter's 'I'm', turned round by 'backing', is taken in by 'receiving'.
explanation.definitionFit: To admire someone is to hold them in high regard, so the verb means to respect.

clue.text: Hopelessness of the French demeanour under pressure

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means placed below the previous piece

parts.note: des is French for 'of the' with a plural noun
P is the abbreviation for pressure in physics
an air is a manner or demeanour

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's bearing betrays his hopelessness when he is under strain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' puts AIR below P in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Despair is the complete loss of hope, so it means hopelessness.

clue.text: Lifeless King's body finally left by the Queen

parts.note: the body of the word king is its middle, the letters I and N
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A dead monarch's corpse is ultimately abandoned by his queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King's body' suggests a corpse, but it means the inside of the word King.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inert is motionless and without life or activity, so it is lifeless.

clue.text: Making certain call provides new basis for result

indicators.note: in a down clue the basis is the bottom letter, which is swapped for the new piece

parts.note: to ensue is to follow or result
to ring someone is to call them on the phone

explanation.surface: A decisive phone call lays new foundations for the outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'provides new basis for' replaces the last E of ENSUE, its base in a down answer, with RING.
explanation.definitionFit: Ensuring something means guaranteeing it will happen, so it is making certain.

clue.text: Specific material used for construction

definitions.meaning: definite and particular rather than vague
the building material made of cement, sand, gravel and water

explanation.surface: A precise description of a building material.
explanation.definitionFit: Concrete means definite or particular, and it is also the hard building material poured into moulds.

clue.text: State lacking any sense working to stop dissemination of union's success

indicators.note: to stop is to plug a gap, so the next piece is placed inside the shuffled letters
dissemination is a scattering, so the letters of union's success are spread about and reordered

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe, then rearranged
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: A trade union's triumph spreads, but some workers are left without any sense of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' suggests labour, fitting the union surface, but just gives a short word; 'dissemination of' jumbles the union phrase and 'to stop' plugs it in.
explanation.definitionFit: Unconsciousness is the condition of being senseless, insensible to anything around you.

clue.text: Stage performer provoked a stir and emptied theatre

indicators.note: provoked means stirred up, so the letters of a stir are shaken into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

indicators.note: an emptied word has lost its contents, leaving only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An actor caused such a commotion that the audience walked out of the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'provoked' rearranges ASTIR into ARTIS; 'emptied' leaves the T and E of theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: An artiste is a professional entertainer such as a singer or dancer who works on stage.

clue.text: Threat posed by introduction of Calor gas

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its opening letter
posed means arranged or set in position, so the letters of threat are set in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Bringing in Calor bottled gas creates a safety threat.
explanation.walkthrough: Calor is a British brand of bottled gas, which makes 'gas' look like part of the scene rather than the definition; 'posed' rearranges the threat.
explanation.definitionFit: Gas as a noun is idle talk, the same as chatter or natter.

clue.text: Ingredient that's specially cut and ground

indicators.note: ground means crushed, so the remaining letters are broken up and reordered
a cut word loses its tail, here the final letter

parts.note: taken as written, then shortened and rearranged

explanation.surface: A cooking ingredient is described as specially chopped and milled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' drops the Y from specially, and 'ground' rearranges SPECIALL into the answer. The surface fits the spice, which is sold ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Allspice is a dried berry used as a spice in cooking, so it is one ingredient of many dishes.

clue.text: Criminal sinned when stealing church's cross

indicators.note: stealing means taking in, so the church goes inside the shuffled letters
criminal means crooked, so the letters of sinned are twisted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A felon who sinned by stealing a church crucifix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like a crucifix but means angry; 'Criminal' jumbles sinned and 'when stealing' takes in the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Incensed means enraged, so it is a strong form of cross in the sense of angry.

clue.text: Steal from fashionable man

parts.note: to steal from someone is to rob them
something fashionable is in

explanation.surface: A man is told to take things from the trendy crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man' is the definition: a man's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin is a common male first name, so it can stand for a man.

clue.text: Footballer inadvertently tackles dancer

indicators.note: to tackle is to grab hold of, so the words hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: A footballer accidentally brings down a dancer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tackles' looks like football, but signals letters held inside 'Footballer inadvertently'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballerina is a female ballet dancer.

clue.text: Tailor item in sale acquired by nouveau riche

indicators.note: acquired means taken in, so the auction item goes inside the shuffled letters
nouveau is French for new, so the letters of riche are made anew in a different order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
a lot is an item put up in an auction sale

explanation.surface: A newly rich person buys an auction lot to get a suit made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nouveau riche' reads as one phrase but splits: 'nouveau' rearranges riche, and 'acquired by' sets the sale item inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailor makes clothes, and a clothier is someone who makes or sells clothing.

clue.text: Person valuing limited company could be auditor's mortgage provider

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so the word is as heard rather than as spelt

parts.note: a lender who provides a mortgage is a loaner

explanation.surface: An accountant checking the books spots who lent money to a small firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'auditor' looks like an accountant, but it means a hearer, signalling a word that sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who keeps to themselves values only limited company, preferring to be alone.

clue.text: Determination to repeat what you wish to do

parts.note: the prefix re- means again, so it is used to repeat an action
a crossword solver wishes to solve the clue

explanation.surface: A person needs resolution to keep doing what they want to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what you wish to do' addresses the solver, whose aim is to solve this puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolve is firmness of purpose, so it means determination.

clue.text: Convincing conclusions of diplomatic dossier fit for public consumption

indicators.note: the conclusions of words are their final letters

parts.note: food fit to be eaten is edible

explanation.surface: The findings of an embassy report are persuasive and suitable for publication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fit for public consumption' usually means suitable to publish; here it is read literally as safe to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A credible story is believable, one that persuades its hearers.

clue.text: Blow up lines following shelling around plain

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the shelled letters go round the next piece
shelling strips the outer casing, so the word lines loses its first and last letters

parts.note: a plain is flat land, so plain means flat

explanation.surface: A city's lines are bombarded after artillery fire across open land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shelling' looks like gunfire, but 'following shelling' strips the outside letters from lines; 'around' wraps them round the plain.
explanation.definitionFit: To inflate a balloon or tyre is to fill it with air, so it means to blow it up.

clue.text: Appropriate time to realise when account's been hacked

indicators.note: hacked means chopped off, so the letters for account are cut away

parts.note: to realise an ambition is to achieve it
AC is short for account

explanation.surface: A good moment to cash in once a bank account has been compromised by hackers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' looks like an adjective but is the verb to take; 'been hacked' cuts the account abbreviation out of the word for realise.
explanation.definitionFit: To appropriate something is to take it for oneself without permission, which is to steal.

clue.text: Crime close to cricket ground

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

parts.note: grounds for doing something are reasons, so ground means reason

explanation.surface: An offence takes place near a cricket pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' suggests a sports venue, but it means a reason or basis.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason, betraying one's country or sovereign, is a serious crime.

clue.text: Raised fortune by end of June to much acclaim

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: X means 'by' as in multiplication or dimensions, as in three by four

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means read upwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: a lot is one's fortune or fate

explanation.surface: Someone's wealth grew by the end of June, to widespread applause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' turns LOT upwards to make TOL in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise highly, so it means to acclaim much.

clue.text: Recalled slave interrupting that woman to update display?

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the whole assembly is read backwards
interrupting means breaking into, so the slave goes inside the word for that woman

parts.note: that woman is her
a serf was a feudal slave bound to the land

explanation.surface: A servant is called back from bothering a lady to change what is on show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' turns round the whole assembly, not just the slave, once 'interrupting' has put him inside that woman. The question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: To refresh a screen or web page is to redraw it with the latest content, updating what is shown.

clue.text: Speech laid bare relationship between two figures

indicators.note: laid bare means stripped, so the speech word loses its outer letters

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: A frank address reveals how two public figures really get on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid bare' strips the outer O and N from ORATION. 'figures' suggests people, but means numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio expresses how two quantities compare, such as three to one, so it relates two numbers.

clue.text: Perhaps overthink cryptic clues a little in English

indicators.note: cryptic means obscure or puzzling, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A solver warns against overanalysing puzzle clues, even slightly, in English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cryptic' rearranges CLUESALITTLEIN into INTELLECTUALIS, followed by E.
explanation.definitionFit: Overthinking is one example of treating something in an overly cerebral, theoretical way, hence the 'Perhaps'.

clue.text: Help whistleblower to suppress story

indicators.note: to suppress is to hold down or contain, so the story is kept inside the referee

parts.note: a referee, ref for short, blows the whistle in a match
a story is a lie or fib

explanation.surface: Someone seeks support for an informant trying to stop a news report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whistleblower' suggests an informant, but it is a match official.
explanation.definitionFit: Relief is aid or assistance given to those in need, so it means help.

clue.text: Average cost of fashion?

parts.note: a mode is a fashion or style
a rate is a price or cost charged

explanation.surface: A shopper asks what fashion typically costs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' links: the fashion's cost is MODE then RATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something moderate is middling or ordinary, neither large nor small, so it is average.
